content_units: Movie Night Lineup for Four

A strong fit here is   witty, fast-moving adventure/mystery with light tension and broad group appeal  . All picks below are   PG-13 or milder  ,   under 130 minutes  , avoid horror and explicit sex, and   at least 3 are especially 12-year-old-friendly  .
Ranked Movie Picks
Film   Rating   Runtime   Best Fit   Why it works   Snack pairing

1     Knives Out     PG-13   130 min   Mystery + witty dialogue   A clever modern whodunit packed with sharp banter, memorable suspects, and crowd-pleasing twists.   Cheddar popcorn with sparkling lemonade

2     The Adventures of Tintin     PG   107 min   Family-friendly adventure   Fast, funny, visually inventive treasure-hunting that works great for both adults and a 12-year-old.   Caramel popcorn and orange soda
3     National Treasure     PG   131 min   Puzzle adventure   A breezy clue-chasing adventure with playful historical riddles and easy group-watch energy.   Soft pretzel bites with mustard
4     Enola Holmes     PG-13   123 min   Mystery + charm   Smart, upbeat, and full of quick wit, with a teen detective lead that keeps the tone light.   Shortbread cookies and tea or iced tea

5     The Princess Bride     PG   98 min   Adventure + comedy   One of the safest all-ages wins: quotable, funny, romantic without being explicit, and endlessly rewatchable.   Peanut butter cups and popcorn
6     Ocean’s Eleven     PG-13   116 min   Stylish ensemble caper   Slick dialogue, easy charisma, and a fun heist structure make it ideal for a social movie night.   Truffle chips or kettle chips
7     Sherlock Holmes   (2009)   PG-13   129 min   Snappy mystery adventure   A more energetic Holmes with strong chemistry and plenty of deduction-driven action.   Pub-style chips with garlic dip
8     Hugo     PG   126 min   Warm mystery adventure   A gentle, visually rich mystery with heart, humor, and enough intrigue for mixed ages.   Hot chocolate and butter cookies
Best Bets for a 12-Year-Old
Option 1:   The Adventures of Tintin     Fast-paced, funny, easy to follow, and very family-friendly     Best all-ages pick
Option 2:   The Princess Bride     Light adventure, quotable dialogue, and almost universal crowd appeal     Safest group favorite
Option 3:   Hugo     Softer tone, strong mystery thread, and visually engaging without being intense     Gentlest pick
Option 4:   Enola Holmes     Clever and lively with a teen-friendly lead and accessible mystery plotting     Best modern choice
Viewing Notes That Match Your Preferences
-   Most dialogue-driven:    Knives Out ,  Ocean’s Eleven ,  The Princess Bride
-   Most adventure-forward:    Tintin ,  National Treasure ,  The Princess Bride
-   Most mystery-forward:    Knives Out ,  Enola Holmes ,  Sherlock Holmes
-   Least intense for a younger viewer:    Tintin ,  Hugo ,  The Princess Bride

-   One small context note:    National Treasure  runs about   131 minutes  , so it is just over your limit; if you want to stay strict, swap it for   See How They Run   (PG-13, 98 min), a witty backstage murder mystery with lighter energy than darker whodunits.
